audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 5 and 6 read Skill in both layers while the whys for those rows say Sett, Sett and Yasuo respectively — and the packet chart agrees with the whys.
audit.why: At a 54.05% win rate over 4605 games this is Sett-favoured through the whole laning phase; the flip is two crit items, not first item.
audit.corrected: Sett through First item, Yasuo at 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why credited Sterak's with making Sett near-unburstable in the row that now belongs to Yasuo.
audit.why: Sweeping Blade falls to a 0.1s cooldown at rank 5 and Last Breath blinks 1400 units to any airborne enemy — his 2-item power is mobility and crit, which Sterak's does not answer.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to state the 0.1s dash and the Wind Wall reality.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six fields told the player to bait, respect or play around Wind Wall — 'bait the wall first', 'Bait Windwall before committing W Haymaker', 'windwall your engage tools', 'walls your engage', 'Save Windwall for your R or key W', and 'where his Windwall and mobility matter least'.
audit.why: Wind Wall blocks projectiles only. Sett's kit contains no projectile at all: Knuckle Down is an empowered attack, Haymaker punches an area, Facebreaker is a pull, and The Show Stopper is a carry-and-slam. None of it is stopped by the wall. Telling a Sett player to wait out a 25s Wind Wall costs him the trade for nothing.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall is now stated as irrelevant to Sett's kit, and the real timer — Steel Tempest's flat 4s and Last Breath's airborne requirement — replaces it.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Last Breath and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Two crit items and Sweeping Blade at 0.1s let him dance around you. Wind Wall blocks projectiles — you have none, so walk through it.

edits.before: - Yasuo Last Breath: matchup-defining — His all-in after a knockup. While down, you win. Track it before every engage. - Yasuo Wind Wall: A wall that blocks all enemy projectiles for a few seconds. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Yasuo Last Breath (R): 70s to 30s — it needs an airborne target, so it only lands off his own Steel Tempest knockup or an ally's CC. - Yasuo Wind Wall (W): 25s, blocks projectiles for 4s — none of your abilities are projectiles.

edits.before: At 2+ items Yasuo's crit power, kiting, and Windwall flip the matchup in his favour.
edits.after: At 2+ items Yasuo's crit power and 0.1s Sweeping Blade dashes flip the lane in his favour.

edits.before: With E Facebreaker up you can walk Yasuo down through his E Sweeping Blade dashes and pull him in; every trade builds Grit, and W Haymaker off a full bar chunks him hard. He can't windwall your point-blank W the moment it fires, so bait the wall first with an auto or Q.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks projectiles and Sett has none — Facebreaker, Haymaker and The Show Stopper all walk straight through it, so never wait for the wall. Walk him down through Sweeping Blade, pull him in, and cash a full Grit bar; every trade he takes feeds the next Haymaker.

edits.before: Yasuo scales into a crit carry who can dance around you with double E dashes, windwall your engage tools, and R off any ally knockup — this is where the matchup flips to him if the fight goes long.
edits.after: Yasuo scales into a crit carry who dances around you on 0.1s Sweeping Blade and blinks in on any ally knockup from 1400 range — Wind Wall never touches your kit, but his mobility does.

edits.before: This is your window — E-pull, W with a fat Grit bar, and at 6 add R to lock a kill. Force short trades where his Windwall and mobility matter least, and don't chase into his wave where he gets free E dashes.
edits.after: This is your window — E-pull, W with a fat Grit bar, and at 6 add R to lock a kill. Steel Tempest is a flat 4s, so trade in the gap after he throws it, and don't chase into his wave where Sweeping Blade is free.

edits.before: Once Yasuo finishes crit items he kites, walls your engage, and ults off any teammate's knockup; end the game before he gets there or fight only when your E is guaranteed to land.
edits.after: Once Yasuo finishes crit items he kites you with 0.1s dashes and blinks 1400 units onto any teammate's knockup; end the game before that, or fight only when Facebreaker is guaranteed to land.

edits.before: Bait Windwall before committing W Haymaker or ignite
edits.after: Punch through Wind Wall — Haymaker is not a projectile

edits.before: Save Windwall for your R or key W
edits.after: Wall off your jungler, not you

edits.before: Keep Sweeping Blade stacks to reposition and kite
edits.after: Chain Sweeping Blade through minions to kite you

notes: The biggest defect in this matchup was six separate Wind Wall instructions, all of which are non-interactions: Sett has no projectile in his kit. Ignite is also not a projectile, so the old 'bait Windwall before ignite' line was wrong twice over. Whether Sett's R suppression can be Wind Walled is moot for the same reason and was not asserted.
